Organization.title: Organization
Organization.description: Represents an organization within the HelmLogic ecosystem, which can be a parent company or a sub-dealer.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Organization entity.

name.description: The official name of the organization.

type.description: The type of the organization, e.g., 'Parent', 'SubDealer'.

parentOrganizationId.description: Reference to the ID of the parent organization, if this organization is a sub-dealer. (Relationship: Organization 1:N Organization)

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the organization record was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the organization record was last updated.

Vessel.title: Vessel
Vessel.description: Represents a maritime vessel managed within the HelmLogic application, including its status and ownership.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Vessel entity.

name.description: The name or model of the vessel.

serialNumber.description: A unique serial or hull number for the vessel.

status.description: The current status of the vessel, e.g., 'On Order', 'In Stock', 'Reserved', 'Sold', 'In Transit'.

organizationId.description: Reference to the ID of the Organization that currently owns or has ordered this vessel. (Relationship: Organization 1:N Vessel)

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the vessel record was created.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the vessel record was last updated.

VesselReservation.title: VesselReservation
VesselReservation.description: Represents a request by a sub-dealer to reserve an 'on order' vessel for a customer.

id.description: Unique identifier for the VesselReservation entity.

vesselId.description: Reference to the ID of the Vessel being requested for reservation. (Relationship: Vessel 1:N VesselReservation)

subDealerOrganizationId.description: Reference to the ID of the sub-dealer Organization making the reservation request. (Relationship: Organization 1:N VesselReservation)

requestedByUserId.description: Reference to the ID of the user (from the sub-dealer organization) who initiated the reservation request. (Relationship: User 1:N VesselReservation)

customerName.description: The name of the end customer for whom the vessel is being reserved.

description.description: An optional description or additional notes provided by the sub-dealer for the reservation request.

status.description: The current status of the reservation request, e.g., 'Awaiting Confirmation', 'Approved', 'Declined', 'Cancelled'.

requestedAt.description: Timestamp when the reservation request was submitted.

processedByUserId.description: Reference to the ID of the user (from the parent organization) who approved or declined the reservation. (Relationship: User 1:N VesselReservation)

processedAt.description: Timestamp when the reservation request was approved or declined.

declineNote.description: An optional note provided by the parent organization user if the reservation request was declined.

Notification.title: Notification
Notification.description: Represents a notification sent to a user within the HelmLogic application, often related to actions like reservation requests or status changes.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Notification entity.

recipientUserId.description: Reference to the ID of the user who is the intended recipient of this notification. (Relationship: User 1:N Notification)

message.description: The detailed message content of the notification.

sourceEntityId.description: The ID of the entity that triggered this notification (e.g., a VesselReservation ID).

sourceEntityType.description: The type of the entity that triggered this notification (e.g., 'VesselReservation').

isRead.description: Indicates whether the recipient user has read the notification.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the notification was generated.

definition.description: Top-level collection for all organizations, including parent companies and sub-dealers. Access is restricted based on membership and roles within the specific organization. Includes a conceptual 'members' map or linkage to the '/users' collection for authorization.

params.name: organizationId
params.description: The unique identifier of the organization.

definition.description: Conceptual collection (derived from application requirements, not explicitly in provided schema) to store user profiles, their associated organization ID (`organizationId`), their parent organization ID (`parentOrganizationId`, if they are part of a sub-dealer organization), and their roles within the organization. This data is critical for DBAC and authorization independence, allowing security rules to perform a single lookup to establish user context.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user (matching Firebase Authentication UID).

definition.description: Top-level collection for all maritime vessels. Each document explicitly includes the `organizationId` of the owning organization for direct ownership-based authorization. Sub-dealers can list 'On Order' vessels belonging to their parent organization.

params.name: vesselId
params.description: The unique identifier of the vessel.

definition.description: Top-level collection for all sub-dealer vessel reservation requests. Includes denormalized 'subDealerOrganizationId' (the requesting sub-dealer), 'vesselOwnerOrganizationId' (the parent organization owning the vessel), and 'vesselStatus' (e.g., 'On Order') for complete authorization independence and simplified security rules. This allows both sub-dealers and parent organizations to manage reservations without 'get()' operations on other collections.

params.name: reservationId
params.description: The unique identifier of the vessel reservation request.

definition.description: Subcollection under each user document to store personal notifications. Access is strictly limited to the user specified by the `userId` in the path, ensuring privacy and enabling secure list operations.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user who is the recipient of the notification.

params.name: notificationId
params.description: The unique identifier of the notification.

firestore.reasoning:
The proposed Firestore data structure prioritizes Authorization Independence and Queryable Authorization Policies (QAPs) by strategically denormalizing authorization context and segregating data by security posture. 

**Authorization Independence:**
1.  **Organization Membership/Roles:** A conceptual `/users/{userId}` collection (though not explicitly provided in the entity schemas, it's essential for DBAC) will store a user's `organizationId`, `parentOrganizationId` (if applicable), and `roles` (e.g., `orgAdmin: true`, `dealerUser: true`). This allows Firestore rules to perform a single `get(/users/$(request.auth.uid))` to retrieve all necessary authorization context for the authenticated user, without needing to traverse document hierarchies. 
2.  **Vessel Ownership:** Each document in the `/vessels/{vesselId}` collection explicitly contains an `organizationId` field, directly indicating the owning organization. This eliminates the need for rules to perform `get()` operations on parent `Organization` documents to determine ownership, making vessel access rules atomic and performant.
3.  **Vessel Reservation Authorization (CRITICAL):** The `/vesselReservations/{reservationId}` collection is designed with significant denormalization to ensure complete authorization independence. Each `VesselReservation` document will denormalize both the `subDealerOrganizationId` (the organization initiating the request) and `vesselOwnerOrganizationId` (the parent organization that owns the vessel and must approve the reservation). This means that rules for creating, reading, updating, or deleting `VesselReservation` documents can evaluate permissions solely based on the data within the `VesselReservation` document itself and the user's `request.auth` context (obtained from the `/users/{userId}` lookup), without requiring any `get()` operations on the related `Vessel` or `Organization` documents.
4.  **Notifications:** Notifications are stored in a subcollection `/users/{userId}/notifications/{notificationId}`. This path-based ownership ensures that access to notifications is strictly limited to the `userId` specified in the path, matching `request.auth.uid`, making them authorization independent and private to the user.

**Queryable Authorization Policies (QAPs):**
1.  **Organizations:** While a general `list` for all organizations is typically not required, specific organization data (e.g., a user's own organization) can be retrieved securely using `where id == request.auth.organizationId` (after a `/users/{userId}` lookup).
2.  **Vessels:** 
    *   Parent organizations can securely `list` all their vessels using `db.collection('vessels').where('organizationId', '==', request.auth.organizationId)`.
    *   Sub-dealers can securely `list` 'On Order' vessels from their parent organization using `db.collection('vessels').where('organizationId', '==', request.auth.parentOrganizationId).where('status', '==', 'On Order')`. Both queries rely on indexed fields, making them efficient and secure without rule filtering.
3.  **Vessel Reservations:** 
    *   Sub-dealers can securely `list` their own reservation requests using `db.collection('vesselReservations').where('subDealerOrganizationId', '==', request.auth.organizationId)`.
    *   Parent organizations can securely `list` reservation requests that require their action using `db.collection('vesselReservations').where('vesselOwnerOrganizationId', '==', request.auth.organizationId).where('status', '==', 'Awaiting Confirmation')`. These are clear, index-friendly queries.
4.  **Notifications:** The structure `/users/{userId}/notifications/{notificationId}` inherently supports secure QAPs. A user can `list` their own notifications by querying `db.collection('users').doc(request.auth.uid).collection('notifications')`, with rules ensuring `request.auth.uid` matches the `userId` in the path segment.

This design avoids complex rule logic and `get()` calls, leading to simpler, more robust, and debuggable security rules, and ensures that `list` operations are performant and secure from the outset.
